name: Stress Management
description: Support for managing acute and chronic stress, balancing demands, and restoring a sense of calm and control.

immediateActions.title: Box Breathing Reset
instructions: Sit upright and place both feet flat on the floor
Exhale all the air out of your lungs slowly
Inhale through your nose for 4 slow counts
Hold your breath comfortably for 4 counts
Exhale through your mouth for 4 counts
Hold for 4 counts with empty lungs; repeat the box 5 times

immediateActions.title: Desk Release Stretch Sequence
instructions: Stand up, feet hip-width apart, and roll your shoulders back 5 times then forward 5 times
Clasp hands behind your back, straighten arms, and lift gently away from your body for 3 deep breaths
Slowly tilt your head to the left, hold 3 breaths, then to the right, hold 3 breaths
Interlace fingers, turn palms up, and stretch arms overhead, leaning slightly left then right
Fold forward gently from the hips, letting arms hang heavy, and take 5 slow breaths
Roll up slowly one vertebra at a time and notice how your body feels

immediateActions.title: 5-Minute Sensory Reset
instructions: Close your eyes and take 3 deep centering breaths
Wash your hands with cool water and notice the temperature on your skin
Wrap both hands around a cold glass of water and hold it for 30 seconds
Open your eyes and slowly look around the room, noticing objects you have not paid attention to before
Eat one piece of food (fruit, chocolate, nut) as slowly as you can, chewing thoroughly and noticing flavour
Put your hand on your heart and take 3 more breaths before returning to your day

immediateActions.title: Stress Deconstruction List
instructions: Write down everything that currently feels stressful or overwhelming, one item per line
Read through your list and place a star next to items with a deadline within the next 24 hours
Place a circle next to items that are truly within your control right now
For starred+circled items, write ONE tiny next action you can take in the next 2 hours
For items you circled without a star, schedule one 15-minute slot later this week to address them
For items you cannot control, cross them off the list and say aloud: I release what I cannot change

safetyGuidance: Stress is a normal part of life, but when it becomes constant or overwhelming it can affect your health and wellbeing. If stress is interfering with your sleep, relationships, work, or ability to enjoy life, consider speaking with a healthcare provider or a counsellor. Taking steps to manage stress early is an act of care for yourself that makes a real difference.
